_README: AUTHORITATIVE SNAPSHOT of the DecimalAI API's regression-check response
contract. The API is a SEPARATE service that this Action's CI runner CANNOT
reach, so we snapshot the contract here and assert the Action's TS types
match it (tests/backend_contract.test.ts).
WHY THIS EXISTS: without it, a field rename or a new/renamed verdict value on
the server would silently break the customer-facing PR comment and the merge
gate, with nothing red anywhere. This committed snapshot makes that drift fail
CI from either direction: change the TS types OR update this file after a
server change, and the test fails until the two agree.
HOW TO REGENERATE: update this file in the same change that alters the
response. The ground truth is a real response body from
POST /api/v1/regression-check — 'backend_response_keys' is the FULL set of
top-level keys it returns, and the two enums are the complete sets of values
the 'verdict' and 'eval_verdict' fields can take (including values a single
response cannot show you, so read them off the server's value list rather
than off one sample).
The Action's RegressionCheckResponse interface (src/api.ts) declares a SUBSET
of those keys — it ignores what it doesn't render. The test asserts:
- every key the Action's TS REQUIRES is present in backend_response_keys
- both verdict enums match the Action's TS Verdict / EvalVerdict EXACTLY.
Note on 'unverified': it is returned only when a structural change has zero
traces in the window to measure it against, so it shows up in almost no real
responses and is the value most likely to be missed when regenerating.
